History:
• Main complaint: 3-day history of watery diarrhoea with associated central abdominal pain and one episode of vomiting this morning.  
• Onset/duration: Symptoms began 3 days ago; neither improving nor worsening.  
• Frequency: Urgent need to open bowels repeatedly; must stay near toilet.  
• Character of pain: Dull ache in mid-abdomen below umbilicus; mildly tender to self-palpation; partially relieved after bowel movement; no radiation.  
• Vomiting: Single episode after eating fruit; no visible blood (red colour attributed to strawberries). Occasional nausea since.  
• Stool characteristics: No visible blood.  
• Hydration/nutrition: Likely sub-optimal fluid intake; eating less to avoid triggers.  
• Constitutional/associated symptoms: Sweating past 4 days; unsure of fever. No chest pain. Baseline mild exertional dyspnoea due to asthma; otherwise breathing normal. No limitation in walking/talking except proximity to toilet.  
• Triggers/exposures: Unsure; denies obvious spoiled food. Recently switched to a different brand of asthma inhaler (unlikely cause per clinician).  
• Relevant family history: Father died of bowel cancer ~10 years ago → patient anxiety about malignancy.  

Past Medical History:
• Asthma.  
• No other chronic diseases reported.

Allergies:
• NKDA.

Medications:
• Asthma inhaler – brand and dose/route/frequency not documented (recently changed).  
• No other regular medications mentioned.

Physical Examination (video/subjective):
• General: Alert, able to converse in full sentences.  
• Abdomen: Patient-reported mild central tenderness on self-palpation; no localisation elsewhere.  
• No visible or reported rectal bleeding.  
• Cardiopulmonary: No chest pain; breathing at baseline; able to walk/talk.  
• Neurological/mental status: Alert & oriented.  
• Vitals: Not recorded (teleconsult).

Impression:
• Likely acute infectious gastroenteritis with dehydration risk.

Management Plan:
• Oral rehydration: Increase water/fluids; consider oral rehydration salts.  
• Symptomatic care: Small, bland meals as tolerated; rest at home.  
• Avoid antibiotics unless clinically indicated; none prescribed.  
• Red-flag advice: Seek in-person GP review or urgent care if any of the following occur – persistent/worsening abdominal pain, high fever, blood in stool or vomit, signs of dehydration (dizziness, reduced urine), or if no improvement within 24–48 h.  
• Follow-up: Patient to book GP appointment if not better or if concerned, particularly given family history of bowel cancer.

Patient Summary:
48-year-old man with asthma developed 3 days of watery diarrhoea, mild mid-abdominal pain, and a single episode of non-bloody vomiting. Clinical picture most consistent with acute gastroenteritis; no alarm features noted. Advised hydration and monitoring; to seek face-to-face review if symptoms persist or worsen.

Key Takeaways:
• Drink plenty of fluids; consider oral rehydration solutions.  
• Stay home, rest, and avoid anti-diarrhoeal antibiotics unless medically directed.  
• Seek medical attention if fever, blood in stool, increased pain, or no improvement within 1–2 days.

Next Steps:
• Monitor symptoms over next 24–48 h.  
• Arrange GP appointment if no improvement or earlier if red-flag symptoms develop.  
• Future consideration: Routine screening for colorectal cancer per guidelines due to family history.
